_comment: The turbulence model catalogue (FR-VVT3). Data, not code: 'model
availability is read from the version manifest, not hard-coded', and
tools/check_version_literals.py keeps it that way.
Each model carries what the advisor must be able to say about it (FR-VVT2):
what it is good at, where it is known to fail, and its relative cost. A
shortlist without those is a single silent answer with extra steps.
'since' names the earliest supported release that ships the model, so a
model absent from the installed version is unselectable rather than merely
warned about. Omitted where the model has been present throughout.
'wall' says which wall treatments the model can be used with. A low-Re
model on a wall-function mesh is the mismatch FR-VVT8 exists to catch, and
the coupling in FR-VVT4 is what makes it unsaveable in the first place.
'baseline' is how broadly applicable a model is when nothing in the
questionnaire distinguishes the candidates. Without it the top pick fell
out of alphabetical order — an arbitrary choice presented authoritatively,
which is what FR-VVT2 forbids. The prior carries its own stated reason, so
a shortlist is never silent about why its leader leads.
'block' is where OpenFOAM stores the model, which is not the same as the
family: hybrid RANS-LES models are declared under `simulationType LES` with
`LESModel`, verified against the motorBike DES tutorial. Writing them into
a RAS block would produce a case that does not run.

wall_functions.label: Wall functions
wall_functions.description: The near-wall layer is modelled, not resolved. Far cheaper, and the standard choice for an industrial mesh.

resolved.label: Resolved near-wall (low-Re)
resolved.description: The viscous sublayer is meshed. Needed for heat transfer, transition and separation onset, and far more expensive.

families.RAS: Reynolds-averaged. One steady or unsteady solution of the mean flow; the cheapest option and the usual starting point.
families.LES: Large-eddy simulation. Resolves the large turbulent structures and models the rest. Inherently unsteady and expensive.
families.hybrid: RANS near walls, LES away from them. Cheaper than LES for external aerodynamics, with its own well-known grey-area problems.

models.name: kEpsilon
models.good_at: Confined flows without strong pressure gradients. Robust, well understood, and the historical default.
models.fails_at: Adverse pressure gradients and separation, which it systematically delays or misses. Poor near walls without wall functions.

models.name: realizableKE
models.good_at: Round jets, rotation and mild separation. Fixes the normal-stress realizability defect of standard k-epsilon.
models.fails_at: Still an epsilon-based model near walls; strong adverse pressure gradients remain difficult.

models.name: RNGkEpsilon
models.good_at: Swirling and rapidly strained flows, where the extra strain term helps.
models.fails_at: Can be less stable than standard k-epsilon, and is no better at separation onset.

models.name: LaunderSharmaKE
models.good_at: Low-Reynolds-number flows resolved to the wall, including transitional cases.
models.fails_at: Requires y+ around 1 everywhere. On a wall-function mesh the answer is meaningless.

models.name: kOmega
models.good_at: Near-wall and adverse-pressure-gradient behaviour, integrable to the wall without damping functions.
models.fails_at: Notoriously sensitive to the free-stream omega value, which makes external flows unreliable.

models.name: kOmegaSST
models.good_at: Separation and adverse pressure gradients. Blends k-omega near the wall with k-epsilon outside, avoiding the free-stream sensitivity. The usual default for external aerodynamics.
models.fails_at: Over-predicts separation in some configurations; still a linear eddy-viscosity model, so no normal-stress anisotropy.

models.name: kOmegaSSTLM
models.good_at: Laminar-turbulent transition, via the Langtry-Menter transition equations.
models.fails_at: Needs a resolved near-wall mesh and careful inlet turbulence; expensive and easy to misuse.

models.name: SpalartAllmaras
models.good_at: External aerodynamics at mild incidence. One equation, cheap and robust.
models.fails_at: Free shear flows and massive separation; no account of transition.

models.name: v2f
models.good_at: Near-wall anisotropy and heat transfer, without needing damping functions.
models.fails_at: Numerically delicate and demanding of the mesh.

models.name: LRR
models.good_at: Flows where normal-stress anisotropy matters — swirl, secondary flows in ducts.
models.fails_at: Seven transport equations, slower and less robust to converge.

models.name: SSG
models.good_at: As LRR, with a better pressure-strain model.
models.fails_at: Same cost and robustness penalty as any Reynolds-stress model.

models.name: Smagorinsky
models.good_at: Free shear flows, as the simplest LES subgrid model.
models.fails_at: Does not vanish at a wall without damping, so wall-bounded flows need care.

models.name: WALE
models.good_at: Wall-bounded LES; the eddy viscosity vanishes at the wall by construction.
models.fails_at: Still needs a genuinely LES-resolved mesh in all three directions.

models.name: kEqn
models.good_at: LES with a transported subgrid energy, which handles non-equilibrium better.
models.fails_at: As with all LES, the mesh cost dominates.

models.name: dynamicKEqn
models.good_at: LES where the model coefficient should adapt rather than be assumed.
models.fails_at: More expensive again, and the dynamic procedure can be fragile.

models.name: SpalartAllmarasDDES
models.good_at: Massively separated external flow at a fraction of LES cost.
models.fails_at: Grey-area and grid-induced separation if the mesh is built carelessly.

models.name: SpalartAllmarasIDDES
models.good_at: As DDES, with wall-modelled LES in the boundary layer.
models.fails_at: Mesh requirements are stricter still, and the same grey area applies.

models.name: kOmegaSSTDES
models.good_at: Separated flow where the RANS branch should be SST rather than Spalart-Allmaras.
models.fails_at: Same grey-area concerns as any DES.
